# TableOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for [`Table`](table.md). Intersects [`BorderedElementOptions`](bordered-element-options.md).

`columns`, `rows`, `header` and `footer` are synthetic sugar, not properties: column weights are constructor-only (`columnWeights` is private readonly), and rows/header/footer route through `addRow` / `addHeader` / `addFooter`.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
type TableOptions = BorderedElementOptions & Partial<Omit<Pick<Table, TableOwnKey>, TableColorKey | 'cellPadding'>> & {
    /** Padding inside every cell. Accepts a length: `5`, `'2mm'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    cellPadding?: LengthInput;
    /** Header row fill. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    headerBackgroundColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Header row text colour. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    headerTextColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Footer row fill. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    footerBackgroundColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Footer row text colour. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    footerTextColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Body row fill. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    rowBackgroundColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Fill for every second data row. */
    alternateRowBackgroundColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Body row text colour. Accepts a palette token or hex. */
    rowTextColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Relative column weights, e.g. `[1, 2, 1]`. Constructor-only sugar. */
    columns?: number[];
    /** Body rows to add, in order. Sugar over {@link Table.addRow}. */
    rows?: TableRow[];
    /** Header row. Sugar over {@link Table.addHeader}. */
    header?: TableRow;
    /** Footer row. Sugar over {@link Table.addFooter}. */
    footer?: TableRow;
}
```

### `border`

```typescript
border?: BorderInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Border widths, and optionally their colour.

Accepts a uniform width, a per-side object, or `{ width, color }`. Omitted sides are zero.

BonniePDF models widths and colours as separate properties (`border` + `borderColors`), so the colour-carrying form resolves to both. The `border` **property setter** deliberately never writes `borderColors` - a setter must not mutate a sibling - which is why this sugar lives here, in the options layer, and is applied by `applyBorderedElementOptions`.

### `borderColors`

borderColors?: BorderColors | undefined

*optional*

Border colors for each side of the element

### `breakAllowed`

```typescript
breakAllowed?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this element can be split across page boundaries. When false, the element is treated as atomic and will be moved to a new page rather than split. If it doesn't fit on a fresh page either, it renders anyway. Default is true.

### `presentation`

```typescript
presentation?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

When `true`, the table is a **layout (presentation) table**: it arranges content in a grid with no tabular data relationships. Per ISO 14289-1 §7.5 / Matterhorn checkpoint 15, such a table MUST NOT be tagged with table structure — so it is tagged as a generic `Div` grouping and each cell's content is tagged with its own natural role in row-major reading order (no `Table`/`THead`/`TR`/`TH`/`TD`, and `addHeader`/`isHeader` are ignored for tagging). Visual output is unchanged. Default `false` (a semantic data table).

Set this for address blocks, totals boxes, and side-by-side panels; keep it `false` for real tabular data (and mark that data's header cells).

### `runningTotalColumn`

```typescript
runningTotalColumn?: number | undefined
```

*optional*

Turns on a running total: the column (0-based, at least 1) that shows it. When the body breaks across pages, each page that continues ends with a "carried forward" row holding the total of the rows' `runningValue` so far, and the next page opens, after any repeated header, with a "brought forward" row holding the same total. The label spans the columns before this one. Both rows are drawn in the footer colours and left out of the accessibility structure, since they repeat what the rows already say. Unset (the default) turns the feature off.

### `runningTotalFormat`

```typescript
runningTotalFormat?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Number format of the running total: `G`, `F<n>`, `N<n>` or `P<n>`, as for charts. Default `'N2'`.
